author: Linnaeus, 1758

art.subject: Common Ringed Plover (Charadrius hiaticula), adult in breeding plumage, as seen on Korean coasts on spring passage in May: white forehead with a black band across the forecrown above it; crown and nape plain grey-brown; black mask from the bill base through the eye to the ear coverts, with a small white mark behind the eye; white throat joining a complete white collar; broad, complete black breast band; upperparts plain grey-brown; underparts white; bill short, orange with a black tip; no obvious coloured eye-ring; legs orange.
art.pose: running on wet sand and stopping to pick prey from the surface, side view
art.scene: Korean west-coast sandy shore at the edge of a tidal flat in May, low tide, soft morning light; no people, buildings or text
art.build: Small, compact, round-headed plover, slightly smaller than a starling and chunkier than Little Ringed Plover, with a short thick neck and horizontal stance. Bill short and stubby, clearly shorter than the head, straight. Legs medium length, orange. In flight a long, clear white wing-bar on brown upperwings, and a brown tail centre with white sides. Runs in short bursts, stops, then tilts forward to pick prey from the surface.
avoid: Do not paint a bright yellow eye-ring or an all-dark bill; that is Little Ringed Plover (Charadrius dubius), which also lacks the white wing-bar.
Do not break the black breast band into two side patches; that is Kentish Plover (Charadrius alexandrinus).
Do not paint dull pinkish or greyish legs; breeding adults have orange legs.
Do not draw a long, slim bill with brown ear coverts; that is Long-billed Plover (Charadrius placidus).
